case.initial_facts:
A patient has bilateral leg weakness and spastic paraplegia, reduced pinprick sensation below T3–T4 and occasional urinary incontinence over two years, with worsening during the last year. Earlier clinicians labelled the illness multiple sclerosis or myelitis.
Brain imaging shows punctate-to-patchy white-matter abnormalities, with sparing of the corpus callosum, cerebellum and brainstem. Spinal imaging shows a symmetric, long-segment ring-like white-matter pattern, relatively sparing central grey matter. CSF cellularity and IgG index are normal, and oligoclonal bands are negative. Age, family history and genetic results are not supplied.

case.decision_point: Assess only the information and task actually supplied at this point.
case.hidden: The source later associates the syndrome with PLAAT4 variants using family/genetic and functional work. Those results, the gene name and cohort summary were not supplied. The reported absence of enhancement in the paper concerns P2, not an established P1 finding.
case.reference: Integrate a progressive spinal-predominant syndrome and the atypical imaging rather than accepting the prior label automatically. An acquired inflammatory cause and inherited/metabolic white-matter disease are defensible categories to discuss; negative oligoclonal bands alone do not establish or exclude a diagnosis. Family history and targeted genetic/other specialist investigation can be proposed without naming the hidden gene. Keep the patient-specific evidence separate from group summaries; age and enhancement status remain unreported.
